newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban warn Shi'ite leader to surrender or fight.
newsitem.headline: Taleban warn Shi'ite leader to surrender or fight.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban militia warned its Shi'ite Moslem rivals on Tuesday to surrender or face an assault on the central province of Bamiyan, a Shi'ite stronghold.

"We have made it clear to Khalili that he should hand over all his weapons and leave Bamiyan or face a battle with our forces," a Taleban front-line commander, Maulvi Abdul Wahid, told reporters at the foot of the Shibar pass leading to Bamiyan.
Karim Khalili leads the Hezb-i-Wahdat faction within an alliance opposed to the purist Sunni Moslem Taleban. Bamiyan, 220 km (138 miles) Northeast of Kabul, is his main bastion.
The Taleban were negotiating with Khalili fighters still guarding the Shekhali Valley leading to Shibar pass. After two hours of talks, Khalili's men agreed to lay down their guns.

Dozens of Taleban fighters then moved in, placing tanks and artillery about three km (two miles) from the crest of the pass. Some came on foot with sleeping bags, many of them from the Ghorband valley to the east, which the Taleban seized last week.
"'We will start our operation as soon as our military council gives the order to march towards Bamiyan," Wahid said.
In Ghorband valley, the Taleban had set up a checkpoint to search southbound vehicles for guns.

The strategic Shibar Pass, now covered in snow, commands the route westward to Bamiyan and also gives access to the long Daraye Shikari gorge leading to northern provinces controlled by ethnic Uzbek General Abdul Rashid Dostum.
Dostum and former government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood belong to the anti-Taleban alliance.
"The people of Daraye Shikari have already fluttered the white flag, and we are confident of capturing Shibar Pass by force if Khalili does not give up," Wahid said.
